answer: Persistent identity escrow: each identity must keep a small deposit locked for a fixed term, and any new identity created after dawn inherits a waiting period before it can transact. The escrow is released only after sustained honest activity, so a clone farm pays the full deposit per identity and forfeits it on detection. Attackers also bear the velvet cost of idle capital across every clone during the waiting period. Scaling to a dune-sized swarm multiplies that locked capital linearly, making mass cloning more expensive than operating one honest identity.
